title: Sanitary Tee Orientation on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a frequent installation mistake in DWV systems. A sanitary tee features a short sweep designed primarily for transitioning fluid from horizontal to vertical flow. When installed horizontally, its short turn disrupts liquid velocity and causes solid waste to accumulate, significantly increasing the likelihood of persistent blockages. Model plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend, or a long-sweep wye fitting, to maintain proper flow dynamics along horizontal runs. Always consult local plumbing codes to verify approved fitting sweeps for specific installation orientations.

Sanitary Tee Orientation on Horizontal Drain Lines

Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a frequent installation mistake in DWV systems. A sanitary tee features a short sweep designed primarily for transitioning fluid from horizontal to vertical flow. When installed horizontally, its short turn disrupts liquid velocity and causes solid waste to accumulate, significantly increasing the likelihood of persistent blockages. Model plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend, or a long-sweep wye fitting, to maintain proper flow dynamics along horizontal runs. Always consult local plumbing codes to verify approved fitting sweeps for specific installation orientations.
